claims.statement: Mazdutide is a long-acting synthetic oxyntomodulin analog that acts as a dual agonist at the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and the glucagon receptor (GCGR), stimulating insulin secretion and engaging glucagon-receptor-mediated energy expenditure pathways alongside GLP-1 receptor activity.

claims.statement: China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) approved mazdutide on June 27, 2025 for chronic weight management, as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, in adults with obesity (BMI ≥28 kg/m²) or overweight (BMI ≥24 kg/m²) with at least one weight-related comorbidity.

claims.statement: In GLORY-1, a randomized, controlled phase 3 trial in 610 Chinese adults with obesity or overweight-plus-comorbidity, once-weekly mazdutide produced mean body weight reductions of -12.05% (4 mg) and -14.84% (6 mg) at 48 weeks versus -0.47% with placebo; 50.6% of participants on 6 mg achieved ≥15% weight loss versus 2.1% on placebo.

context.useCase: chronic weight management (pivotal trial supporting NMPA approval)
context.doseText: 4 mg or 6 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 48 weeks (trial protocol, matches approved regimen; not a use recommendation)

claims.statement: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial (n=250) in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, mazdutide 3-6 mg weekly for 20 weeks reduced HbA1c by -1.41% to -1.67% (dose-dependent) versus +0.03% with placebo and -1.35% with dulaglutide 1.5 mg (all mazdutide doses P<0.0001 vs placebo); body weight fell up to -7.1% with mazdutide versus -1.4% with placebo.

context.population: Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, n=250
context.formulation: mazdutide 3 mg, 4.5 mg, or 6 mg (active comparator: dulaglutide 1.5 mg)
context.useCase: glycemic control in type 2 diabetes (phase 2, investigational at time of trial)
context.doseText: 3 mg, 4.5 mg, or 6 mg subcutaneously once weekly, titrated, for 20 weeks (trial protocol; not a use recommendation)

up to −7.1% with mazdutide (−2.7% with dulaglutide and −1.4% with placebo)

claims.statement: Across mazdutide trials, the most common adverse events are gastrointestinal: diarrhea, decreased appetite, nausea, and vomiting, generally mild-to-moderate; in the phase 2 T2D trial these occurred in 36%, 29%, 23%, and 14% of mazdutide-treated participants respectively, with no GI-related treatment discontinuations, and in GLORY-1 heart-rate increases (~2.6 bpm) were reported without an observed cardiovascular safety signal.

context.population: Chinese adults with obesity/overweight or type 2 diabetes enrolled in phase 2/3 trials

claims.statement: Mazdutide has no FDA approval and is not a legally marketed product in the United States, yet gray-market research-chemical vendors sell it directly to consumers with dosing and self-injection guidance while stating it is for research use only; the strongest available human efficacy and safety evidence comes exclusively from supervised, NMPA-regulated clinical trials in China, and does not establish the safety or effectiveness of unsupervised, vendor-sourced self-administration in other populations.

context.population: US and other non-China consumers purchasing peptide products online
context.useCase: self-administered weight loss / diabetes management outside supervised clinical or approved-product settings

conflicts.summary: NMPA approval claims rely on company (Innovent) press releases rather than a primary NMPA-hosted regulatory document, since no fetchable official NMPA label/page in English was located in this session; content is consistent across two independent Innovent releases and multiple trade-press secondary reports, but has not been cross-verified against a government-hosted source.

Mazdutide is a fully approved prescription product in China but is simultaneously sold in the US/international gray market as an unapproved 'research chemical'; packet consumers must not conflate the China-approved-product evidence base with the safety/legality of gray-market self-administered product.
